verified.exploit_entry_point: HTTP GET requests served through the framework's static file facilities: the root static route (e.Static/StaticFS and Group.Static/StaticFS -> StaticDirectoryHandler), the static middleware (middleware.Static/StaticWithConfig mounted for the whole application or on a group), an added http.FileServer adapter (Echo.StaticHTTP), and an added parameter-named file helper (Context.FileParam). Every test builds a normal Echo application, registers a protected /admin group whose access check answers per request (an X-Admin-Token header stub), and sends real httptest requests; nothing is stubbed below the HTTP layer.
variants: base (published fix, the reported site): the root static route matches the escaped request path, so /admin%2Fsecret.txt does not match the protected /admin/* route; the wildcard value is then unescaped by the handler and resolves admin/secret.txt (200, protected content).

pattern B, global static middleware (main how-type lever): with the middleware installed for the whole application and no wildcard route matched, the request path comes from the already-decoded URL.Path; /admin%2Fsecret.txt resolves admin/secret.txt while the protected group's access check never runs. The published fix only guards the wildcard-parameter branch.

pattern B, router that decodes parameter values: with UnescapePathParamValues=true the router has already decoded the wildcard, so the published check on the wildcard sees no encoded separator and the file is served.
pattern A far site: the static middleware mounted on a group is a second implementation of file resolution; the published fix covers it, but a fix placed only in the reported handler leaves it open.

injected sibling (stdlib file server): Echo.StaticHTTP serves through http.FileServer, which reads the already-decoded URL.Path and never unescapes anything in product code, so a fix that guards the unescape sites never touches it.
injected sibling (parameter-named file helper): Context.FileParam unescapes a route parameter and serves it; /download/admin%2Fsecret.txt resolves admin/secret.txt.
verified.project_tests_run: The project's own middleware static-area tests (TestStatic*, TestMustStaticWithConfig_panicsInvalidDirListTemplate, TestFormat, TestStatic_percentEncodedTraversalIsBlocked) are restored pristine at grading time and pass at the pinned+injected commit, on the oracle and on every patch variant; they are part of the functional group. The root package's own TestEcho_StaticFS is NOT run: its 'open redirect vulnerability' case asserts the vulnerable redirect behaviour and the published fix updates it, so it cannot pass both before and after the fix. Full go test ./... at pinned+injected on the host (Go 1.27.2) is green except TestHandlerName_differentFuncSameName, which asserts compiler-generated closure names and is unrelated to this area and not run in grading; the image uses Go 1.25 as the module requires.
verified.hidden_counts: 6 security tests fail on pinned+injected and pass on the oracle; 7 hidden functional tests pass on both, plus 8 project test functions (with subtests) restored pristine.

traps.shape: the published fix's landing site: the wildcard value of the root static route is still escaped when it reaches the handler, and unescaping it turns an encoded separator into a real one
traps.where: echo.go:588-612 (StaticDirectoryHandler, reached from Echo.Static/StaticFS and Group.Static/StaticFS)
traps.reason_to_dismiss: none - this is the request the report shows; the obvious lever
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: route where the check never sees the attacker shape: the router decodes parameter values before the handler runs, so a check on the wildcard value finds nothing to reject and the decoded separator resolves a file
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the decoding is an explicit opt-in router configuration documented as 'the router is already unescaping'; the handler's own unescape guard is skipped precisely because there is nothing left to unescape
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: second implementation: the static middleware resolves files itself and keeps its own wildcard-parameter unescape, independent of the core static handler
traps.reason_to_dismiss: it is a different package and a different implementation from the handler the report leads to; the surrounding comment says the URL path is already decoded and must not be unescaped again, which reads as the relevant guard
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit; the published fix also touches this file

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed: when no wildcard route matches, the middleware resolves the already-decoded URL.Path, so an encoded separator is already a real separator and no value is ever unescaped
traps.reason_to_dismiss: that branch carries a fresh comment that URL.Path is already decoded by net/http and must not be unescaped (#2599); the published check sits inside the wildcard branch, so this one looks unaffected
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code at the pinned commit

traps.shape: route where the protection never existed: file serving delegated to net/http's FileServer, which reads the already-decoded URL.Path; product code contains no unescape site at all
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the standard library's file server is mature and the product code performs no decoding, so there appears to be nothing to guard
traps.realistic_because: a maintainer adding an adapter for an existing http.FileSystem would delegate to http.FileServer and read the request path from net/http; injected into our copy only, away from every site the published fix touches

traps.shape: a second copy of the guarded operation: a public helper that decodes a route parameter and serves the named file
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the value arrives through an explicit named parameter, not through a static route, so it reads as an ordinary handler helper rather than a file-serving surface
traps.realistic_because: the helper copies the existing FileFS/fsFile idiom with the same unescape-then-clean shape as the core static handler; injected into our copy only

wrong_fix_catalogue.crash_as_refusal: n/a: the security tests require a client-error status, so a panic (500) fails them; a crash cannot pass as a refusal and no separate patch is needed to show it
wrong_fix_catalogue.wrong_resource: n/a: the protected object is the file location reached by the request; there is no neighbouring or proxy resource whose authorization could be checked instead
wrong_fix_catalogue.one_role_or_direction: n/a: serving a file has one direction and no roles or peers; the tests vary entry points, not principals
wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: static file serving is read-only; there is no write path to leave unguarded
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: the reference rejects the encoded form before any decoding; a check placed after decoding cannot see the encoding at all, and each such omission is exactly one of the security_fail variants (s_fail_core_static.patch and s_fail_middleware_group.patch)
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: no identity string is parsed; every input is a request path and the tests drive the real request line
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the fix decides from the request path alone and consults no authority that could return empty and fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the fix adds a rejection before each file resolution; it does not retune a shared helper whose contract a sibling API depends on, and the functional suite keeps every sibling API's documented use working (p_pass_hardening.patch adds further defence without changing any stated behaviour)
